## Passages
RESULT [attribution]: Selecting data by similarity to 'high quality' sources may not increase performance, and can even hurt it, compared with random selection. DsDm-selected data gave a 2x compute multiplier over baseline selection methods on language-model benchmarks.
US [attribution]: This directly questions the 'DINOv2-similarity filter' step of the base-dataset plan. It matches the project's own sealed M1 result (DINO>=0.50-curated 13.3K -> 0.5894 +/- 0.0025 vs raw 55.7K -> 0.6032 +/- 0.0046). The base dataset should be chosen by measured effect on the holdout metric, e.g. per-slug ablations, not by embedding similarity alone.
CORRECTION [attribution]: The abstract matches: similarity-to-high-quality selection may not help and can hurt vs random, and DsDm gives a 2x compute multiplier over baselines. Venue: the paper was also published at ICML 2024, so 'arXiv' alone undersells it.
